transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-29 15:00 PT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Sophie Patel (Head of Data - Rivergate), Aaron Kim (ML Engineer), Priya Rao (CTO - Platform), Ben Torres (Product), Elaine Wu (Legal)

Summary (auto): scoping call for POC, focus on claims intake and triage, need for Spanish support, tight latency SLO on user-facing chat triage, concern about PHI and residency.

00:00:05 - Maya Chen: All right everyone thanks for joining, uh this is Maya from Redwood, and with me is Luis our solutions engineer. today we wanted to run through the POC scope, the models we're suggesting for open-model tests, and nail down success criteria and timelines.
00:00:18 - Sophie Patel: Hi Maya, thanks. We're excited. Quick background: Rivergate's modernizing claims intake, replacing a set of rules and keyword parsers with a semantic layer to extract claimant info, incident descriptors, policy numbers, and do an initial severity triage.
00:00:35 - Aaron Kim: yeah and we have existing microservices but the ML component is basically a mono model we built last year, it's not robust, lots of hallucinations and can't handle Spanish well. so main ask is: better extraction accuracy and bilingual support.
00:00:52 - Luis Ortega: got it. couple clarifying q's — do you expect user-facing chat with responses to customers, or is this backend-only for agent UI?
00:01:00 - Ben Torres: mostly backend for triage, but we will surface some suggested messages to the claims agent. so latency matters, not ultra low like 10 ms, but we want snappy.
00:01:12 - Sophie Patel: SLA goal we'd like 95th percentile under 400ms for generation+post-processing for agent-facing prompts. for batch extraction jobs 95th under 2s is fine.
00:01:27 - Maya Chen: that's helpful. on data sensitivity — Elaine from legal is here — do you consider transcripts and claim descriptions PHI under your policy?
00:01:35 - Elaine Wu: yes some of it is PHI. for POC we can provide de-identified data but eventual production may require either private deployment or a dedicated instance with strict KMS.
00:01:47 - Luis Ortega: notes, so deployment mode will be discussed — hosted first-run ok with de-id, but we should plan for Dedicated or Private later.
00:01:56 - Aaron Kim: also, traffic profile: peak concurrent ~60 requests per minute, spike to 200 rpm during morning hours. average request size is ~250 tokens, some longer policy-copypaste up to 2k tokens.
00:02:12 - Maya Chen: helpful. for the POC we usually do baseline vs candidate models: we'll run throughput and latency tests plus quality evals on extraction. we have a recommended shortlist but first wanted to confirm your priorities: accuracy first, latency second, cost third?
00:02:27 - Sophie Patel: accuracy, especially precision on extracted entities (policy id, date, claimant name), then low hallucination — false positives are costly for downstream automation.
00:02:38 - Ben Torres: and bilingual capability: English and Spanish coverage is mandatory; French is lower priority.
00:02:47 - Luis Ortega: great. proposed shortlist we suggest for open models: 1) LlamaX-13B quantized — good quality, balanced latency; 2) OrcaLite-7B-int8 — faster, less context; 3) Mosaic-12B-quant — strong multilingual performance. i'll send exact config names in the follow-up.
00:03:10 - Aaron Kim: quick q — how do you handle KV cache and prefix caching for multi-turn? our UI threads have repeated references to policy numbers.
00:03:19 - Luis Ortega: we have prefix/KV cache support, though the transcript auto-transcribe sometimes calls it K V cash, but yes we cache repeated context to reduce cost and improve latency on agent flows.
00:03:29 - Sophie Patel: how are you measuring hallucination? we need something actionable.
00:03:34 - Maya Chen: we typically measure hallucination rate as the proportion of extracted facts that cannot be matched to ground truth within tolerance. for names and policy IDs we use exact match, for narrative fields we use human rating on a sample and an n-gram overlap metric to flag likely hallucinations.
00:03:50 - Aaron Kim: ok, makes sense. and for multilingual evals do you backtranslate or do native speakers annotate?
00:03:56 - Luis Ortega: native speakers for critical fields; backtranslation for quick heuristics. for Spanish we have a small annotator pool.
00:04:05 - Ben Torres: timeline? how long to run baseline?
00:04:09 - Maya Chen: baseline bench typically 1-2 days for throughput and latency at your traffic profile, quality evals take about a week including annotations. for POC we aim for a 4-week loop: week 0 data and test plan, week 1 baseline and candidate runs, week 2 analysis and remediation, week 3 pilot integration.
00:04:29 - Sophie Patel: 4 weeks sounds good. cough, is there wiggle room if we need more annotators?
00:04:35 - Luis Ortega: yes, we can scale annotation or provide more automated heuristics, but that'll affect cost and time.
00:04:42 - Elaine Wu: security questions: SOC2 status, SSO/SAML support, audit logs, and whether Redwood supports customer-managed keys.
00:04:50 - Maya Chen: Redwood's hosted offering is SOC2 compliant, we have SSO/SAML and RBAC in the console, and Dedicated/Private support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest. we'll share the security pack after the call.
00:05:04 - Elaine Wu: great please send the SOC doc and encryption spec.
00:05:08 - Maya Chen: will do.
00:05:11 - Aaron Kim: on benchmarking — what metrics will you run out of the box?
00:05:15 - Luis Ortega: default set: token latency (p50/p95/p99), end-to-end request latency including pre/post processing, throughput at target concurrency, memory/VRAM utilization on nodes, and quality metrics: F1/precision/recall for extractions, exact match for policy id, hallucination rate, and a simple end-to-end intent accuracy.
00:05:33 - Sophie Patel: we need a strong emphasis on exact match for identifiers. false matches are the worst.
00:05:37 - Luis Ortega: noted. we'll add stricter thresholds for policy id.
00:05:40 - Ben Torres: cost signals — how do you present RU per request and projected monthly cost?
00:05:45 - Maya Chen: Redwood Optimize will produce per-route cost estimations based on throughput, batching profile, and KV cache hit rate. we'll model your monthly cost under baseline and peak scenarios.
00:05:56 - Aaron Kim: curious about quantization — what's the tradeoff you expect between 7B int8 and 13B q4?
00:06:02 - Luis Ortega: empirically, 7B-int8 gives much faster latency and lower VRAM, but you may see drops in recall on ambiguous spans. 13B q4 tends to have higher extraction F1 and lower hallucination at the expense of higher latency and cost. we recommend running both as part of POC so you can measure delta on your data.
00:06:20 - Sophie Patel: does Redwood do hybrid routing? like use smaller model for majority then fall back to bigger for high-risk cases?
00:06:26 - Luis Ortega: yes, smart routing is supported — you can route by confidence threshold: low-confidence outputs get re-run on a larger model. that's more complex to set up but reduces cost while preserving quality.
00:06:37 - Ben Torres: that would be ideal for triage — quick pass then escalate certain cases.
00:06:41 - Maya Chen: for the POC we can prototype a two-pass flow: candidate smaller model for initial extraction, and a flagged subset to 13B for verification. we'll include that in the benchmark matrix as an experiment.
00:06:54 - Aaron Kim: excellent. next, data format — we'll send JSONL with fields: text, language, ground_truth_entities. what's the preferred tokenization and do you accept var-length documents?
00:07:04 - Luis Ortega: JSONL is perfect. we expect text and a separate annotations file. we handle variable lengths; for very long docs we'll truncate or use chunking strategies and aggregate. include language tag for each example.
00:07:17 - Sophie Patel: one more thing — policy numbers sometimes come with OCR noise. can you handle fuzzy matching?
00:07:23 - Luis Ortega: yes our evals include fuzzy match thresholds; for policy ids we can tune for edit-distance 1 or 2 depending on OCR error rates.
00:07:31 - Priya Rao: about private deployment — what's the typical timeline and what's involved if we need on-prem later?
00:07:38 - Maya Chen: Private/on-prem has longer lead time — typically 6-10 weeks for packaging and security assessments; Dedicated is faster (2-4 weeks) if you want customer-dedicated GPU pools in the cloud. for POC we usually start hosted with de-id data then move to Dedicated or Private for production.
00:07:55 - Elaine Wu: sounds workable. we'll confirm which path in the next week.
00:07:59 - Maya Chen: ok great. so to be concrete i will send a 3-model shortlist with exact model variants and quant configs, a benchmark matrix that includes the two-pass experiment, and a sample test plan.
00:08:12 - Aaron Kim: when you say model variants — will you include latencies on our traffic profile?
00:08:16 - Luis Ortega: yes we'll include estimated p95 latencies at your concurrency and also run live baseline once we have your dataset.
00:08:22 - Sophie Patel: what about multilingual baseline — will you run the same for English and Spanish?
00:08:26 - Luis Ortega: yes, we'll run separate breakdowns and annotate Spanish with native annotators for key fields.
00:08:31 - Ben Torres: any immediate blockers from your side?
00:08:35 - Priya Rao: none, just internal legal to confirm de-id process.
00:08:39 - Elaine Wu: we'll share the de-id checklist.
00:08:42 - Maya Chen: perfect. i'll summarize the proposed shortlist now at a high level: LlamaX-13B-q4 — good extraction F1, moderate latency; OrcaLite-7B-int8 — best latency and cost; Mosaic-12B-q4 — strongest multilingual recall, slightly more VRAM. these are examples not final names.
00:09:03 - Aaron Kim: that's helpful. any recommendations for prompt engineering for extraction?
00:09:08 - Luis Ortega: short guidance: explicit field instruction, few-shot examples in the prompt for tricky entity types, and use structured output (json) with strict schema so it's easier to validate and post-process. we'll provide a prompt template.
00:09:22 - Sophie Patel: can Redwood host the evaluation harness or do we run locally?
00:09:27 - Maya Chen: both options. we can run the controlled benchmark on Redwood-hosted infra for speed, or we can ship a harness that your team runs in your environment. for PHI we'd recommend your infra or dedicated instance.
00:09:40 - Aaron Kim: we'll probably start hosted with de-id and then run a final on our dedicated environment.
00:09:45 - Ben Torres: budget concerns — we have an upper-bound for the POC. how do you model cost?
00:09:50 - Maya Chen: we'll provide cost estimates for each config and a projected monthly run rate. also show cost delta for two-pass vs single-pass.
00:09:58 - Sophie Patel: ok. any benchmarks externally we can reference?
00:10:02 - Luis Ortega: we have some public bench results on similar extraction workloads; i'll include a one-pager. note will emphasize they are indicative — your data is the true decider.
00:10:12 - Aaron Kim: if we accept the shortlist, what's the concrete POC schedule?
00:10:16 - Maya Chen: proposed schedule: Day 0 (this call) agree dataset + success criteria. By 2026-11-03 Rivergate shares dataset. 2026-11-05 Redwood shares shortlist and bench plan. Week of 2026-11-09 run baseline & candidate runs (2-3 days). 2026-11-16 analysis meeting with results. 2026-11-23 pilot integration if results are good.
00:10:40 - Priya Rao: sounds reasonable.
00:10:43 - Elaine Wu: legal will review PII de-id plan before sending.
00:10:47 - Maya Chen: noted. any other questions?
00:10:51 - Aaron Kim: on the evals will you open-source the harness or is it internal?
00:10:55 - Luis Ortega: we can share the harness and test scripts; some infra pieces are Redwood-managed, but the scoring scripts and prompts we'll provide.
00:11:03 - Sophie Patel: great.
00:11:05 - Maya Chen: i'll put a quick recap in the follow-up email: dataset, success criteria (exact match policy id >= 98%, extraction F1 >= 90% on core fields, hallucination <= 2% on sampled checks, latency p95 < 400ms for agent prompts), shortlist, timeline, and action items.
00:11:24 - Ben Torres: those thresholds look tight but okay for POC.
00:11:28 - Aaron Kim: one more technical question — do you support running tests with different batching configs? we want to measure impact of batching on latency for agent flows.
00:11:36 - Luis Ortega: yes we will test with varying batch sizes and measure batching break-even points given your concurrency. we'll include that in the throughput matrix.
00:11:45 - Maya Chen: okay i think we're aligned. quick note: i'll include estimated VRAM for each model to help you decide whether Dedicated is needed.
00:11:54 - Sophie Patel: final Q — do you support per-route rate limiting in Dedicated?
00:11:59 - Luis Ortega: yes, per-route quota and throttling plus graceful fallback to smaller models is supported.
00:12:05 - Maya Chen: perfect. any other items?
00:12:08 - Priya Rao: none. thanks everyone.
00:12:11 - Maya Chen: thanks, we'll follow up with the docs and the shortlist.

(Transcript continues with quick clarifying points and closing)
00:22:00 - (briefly) Aaron: we'll strip PHI and upload by next Tuesday, Eduardo from ops will help.
00:26:30 - Luis: I'll draft the two-pass experiment details and include confidence threshold suggestions.
00:31:12 - Maya: Elaine we'll attach SOC2 + encryption spec, Sophie we'll include a benchmark matrix and projected costs.
00:40:05 - Sophie: ok looking forward to it.
00:46:30 - Maya: thanks all, end meeting.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (K V cash, model names slightly off), multiple crosstalk sections, speaker tags provided by the recorder and may be imperfect.
